title: Victor S. Miller
name: Victor S. Miller
summary: American mathematician and cryptographer who independently introduced elliptic curves as a basis for public-key cryptography.
whyThisMatters: Miller’s 1985 elliptic-curve proposal became part of the technical basis of ECC, a widely deployed family of public-key systems.
knownFor: Use of elliptic curves in cryptography

sections.overview:
Victor S. Miller is an American mathematician and cryptographer. His 1985 work proposed elliptic curves for public-key cryptography, independently of Neal Koblitz.

Cryptographic legacy

Elliptic-curve cryptography became an important approach to public-key design. Miller’s research also gave rise to the pairing computation commonly known as Miller’s algorithm.

timeline.event: Completes a PhD in mathematics at Harvard University.
Publishes “Use of elliptic curves in cryptography.”
Publishes work on efficient calculation of the Weil pairing.
Receives the Levchin Prize in Real World Cryptography.
